10 January, 2024
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 Civil Revision Petition Nos.1430 and 1555 Of 2019
Common Order:

Aggrieved by the common order dated 29.03.2019 (hereinafter will be referred as 'impugned order')
in I.A.Nos.32 and 33 of 2019 in L.A.O.P.No.11 of 2018 on the file of learned Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad, the claimant No.72 filed the present Civil Revision Petitions to set aside the impugned order.

2. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties will be referred as per their array before the learned Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad.

3. Since both the Civil Revision Petitions are arising out of common order in LAOP No.11 of 2018 and since the subject matter in both the cases is one and the same, this Court is inclined to pass common order in both the Civil Revision Petitions.

4. The brief facts of the case as can be seen from the record available before this Court are that one Vadakapuram 2 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 Damodhara Chary i.e., Claimant No.55 in LAOP No.11 of 2018 along with other claimants i.e., Claimant Nos.47 to 49, 51, 53, 56, 60 to 62, 64 to 66,
67 (died LRs brought on record) and 68 filed I.A.No.32 of 2019 under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to permit them to withdraw compensation to the extent of structures and wells over the lands acquired by the government by reserving their right to contest the claim over the acquired lands as per the procedure.

Similar petition was filed by claimant Nos.26 to 41 vide I.A.No.33 of 2019 under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to permit them to withdraw compensation to the extent of structures and wells over the lands acquired by the government by reserving their right to contest the claim over the acquired lands as per the procedure.

In both the petitions, the contention of the petitioner is that their properties were acquired by the Land Acquisition Officer for formation of '4' lane road in the limits of Algunur Village and at the time of payment of compensation one V. Srinivasa Chary i.e., the revision petitioner herein and claimant No.72 filed objection petition before the Land Acquisition Officer that entire lands acquired in Sy.Nos.501 and 453 belongs to his ancestors and requested the Land Acquisition Officer not to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

Based on the said petition, the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter before the Court 3 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 under Section 77(2) of the Land Acquisition Act (hereinafter will be referred as 'the Act').

It is the contention of the petitioners that the claim of revision petitioner/claimant No.72 is with regard to only lands, however, the Land Acquisition Officer without pursuing the matter had referred the entire property i.e., compensation of lands and other properties before the Court.

sentences.text:
To the above said petitions the revision petitioner/claimant No.72 filed counter, the details of whch are as under:
a) The land in Sy.Nos.501 and 453 belongs to Vadla @ Vadakapuram Rajalingam, the great grandfather of Respondent No.1/revision petitioner and after his death, his legal heirs V. Kistaiah, V. Mallaiah, V. Chandraiah and v. Rajalingu inherited the said property and their names were mentioned in the revenue records as the persons in possession of the land in Sy.Nos.501 and 453.
Subsequently, after their death, the property was inherited by respondent No.1 and other legal heirs.
The respondent No.1 became the absolute owner and possessor of the land admeasuring Ac.6.32 guntas in Sy.No.501 and Ac.1.14 guntas in Sy.No.453 since he purchased the shares of all other legal heirs.

The Government acquired the land of respondent No.1 to an extent of Ac.0.16.36 guntas (1979.56 square yards) in Sy.No.501 and Ac.0.03.60 guntas (435.60 square yards) in Sy.No.453 for the purpose of 4 - way lane road in the limits of Alugunur Village leading from Hyderabad to Ramagundam via Karimnagar.
The names of ancestors of respondent No.1 are mentioned in the revenue records as pattadars of the land.

Since the names of some of the claimants in LAOP No.11 of 2018 were also notified by the government, the respondent No.1 submitted his objections before the Land Acquisition Officer claiming his right over the land in Sy.Nos.501 and 453.

When the Land Acquisition Authorities tried to release the compensation in favour of the persons, whose names were notified in acquisition proceedings, the respondent No.1 filed W.P.No.30564/2015, which is pending.

c) The petitioners are claiming compensation amount in respect of the structures claiming that the structures were raised by them but as a matter of fact all those structures are illegal and unauthorized and respondent No.1 sought for relief of demolition of said structures by filing W.P.No.26304 of 2017.

In the said Writ Petition, the Secretary of Alugunur Gram Panchayath filed counter stating that there are no files available 5 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 in the office relating to the houses claimed by the petitioners.
It is clear that the structures raised in the land in Sy.Nos.501 and 453 are illegal and unauthorized.

The Revenue Divisional Officer made a complaint to the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Karimnagar for taking necessary action against the petitioners/claimants on the ground that they are encroachers of the land.
During the course of award enquiry, there was no mention before the Land Acquisition officer by the claimants herein with regard to the house numbers said to have been allotted to the structures.
Thus, the petitioners are not entitled to receive any compensation and prayed to dismiss the petitions.
6. After considering the rival contentions, the learned Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad has allowed the petitions.
Aggrieved by the same, the respondent No.1/revision petitioner/claimant No.72 has filed the present Civil Revision Petitions to set aside the impugned common order.

sentences.text: 7. Heard both sides and perused the record.

8. The contention of the learned counsel for the revision petitioner is that the structures for which the petitioners/claimants are claiming compensation are illegally 6 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 raised by the petitioners/claimants without any valid permission from the competent authority and thereby they are not entitled for compensation.
It is further contention of the learned counsel for the revision petitioner that the trees and wells are in existence over the subject land to which belongs to revision petitioner.

It is pertinent to note that only after notifying the names of the petitioners/claimants in the preliminary notification and after conducting enquiry in the award proceedings, the names, ownership of structures and the extent of land acquired by the government,
the compensation was awarded for the structures.

Admittedly and even as seen from the preliminary notification under Section 4 (1) of the Act and also the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer,
the names of the claimants in both the interlocutory applications are very much present and the compensation was awarded for the structures over the subject lands.

On the other hand, the revision petitioner has not placed any material either before the learned Land Acquisition Officer or before the learned Tribunal or before this Court, to substantiate his contentions that the structures over the subject lands were raised illegally.

The only ground on which the revision petitioner is opposing the claim of the claimants/petitioners is that the in the said Writ Petition filed by the revision petitioner,
the Secretary of Alugunur Gram 7 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 Panchayath filed counter stating that there are no files available in the office relating to the houses claimed by the petitioners.
Merely because the files were not available in the office, it cannot be said that houses claimed by the petitioners/ claimants were illegally raised.
9. It is not the case of the revision petitioner that he has raised the structures over the subject lands and that they belong to him.
The revision petitioner claimed that the trees and wells were existing on the subject land belongs to him but no material is placed before this Court to establish the same.

Moreover, the revision petitioner is claiming that the structures were raised by the petitioners/claimants illegally and in this regard he has filed Writ before the High Court for demolition of the said structures and the said Writ is pending.

Both the Writs filed by the revision petitioner are pending and mere filing of Writs by the revision petitioners cannot be a ground precluding the trial Court to pass an order, more particularly, when it is not the case of the revision petitioner that some enforceable or injunctive orders were granted by the High Court in the said Writs.

When it is admitted by the revision petitioner that the structures were raised by the claimants, certainly there is no embargo for the trial Court in releasing the compensation for 8 MGP,J Crp_1430 and 1555_2019 the said structures over the subject lands, more particularly, when the revision petitioner has not claimed the compensation for the said structures and in fact he filed Writ seeking demolition of said structures over the subject lands and that indicates that he is not interested in the compensation that was awarded to the structures over the subject lands.

In the impugned order, the trial Court rightly observed that in the counter filed by the Secretary of Gram Panchayath in W.P.No.26304 of 2017 it is stated that even though there were no prior permissions obtained by the petitioners/claimants for construction of the houses, still house numbers were allotted and property tax was collected from the persons in occupation of the said houses.

Even in the award, it was alleged that the RDO/LAO have repeatedly visited the acquired land and after conducting several enquiries and after making several amendments, the names of the persons in Vadla , Vakadapuram Srinivasa Chary vs Mohd. Kareem Bee on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29857271/

sentences.text: Further, except contending that the structures that were raised over the subject lands were illegal constructions, no material is placed by the revision petitioner to establish that the claimants are not entitled for compensation in respect of the structures over the subject lands, that were acquired by the Government for laying '4' lane road in the limits of Algunur Village.

In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the considered view that there is no infirmity or error apparent on the face of record in the impugned order, more particularly, when the scope of revision under Article 227 of the Constitution of India to interfere with the findings of the trial Court is very limited to a supervisory role and can certainly not be the resort to correct every erroneous order.
As seen from the grounds of revision, the revision petitioner failed to bring out any of the grounds showing that there is an error apparent on the face of the record to set aside the impugned order.
Therefore, there are no merits in the Civil Revision Petitions and thereby they are liable to be dismissed.
11. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petitions are dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending Miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
